# Wrong Numbers

> Arthi Arumugam audits LLM evaluation and cost accounting code: eval scores checked against known-answer tests, token and cost metering checked against provider invoices, with every finding delivered as a failing test and its fix. 26 merged upstream fixes across 14 organisations, including inspect_evals (UK AI Security Institute), TruLens (Snowflake), lm-evaluation-harness, Pydantic Logfire and genai-prices, dbt Labs MetricFlow, Mistral, LiveKit, Pipecat, deepset and Roboflow. The recurring defect: the counts look right, the score or the dollars are wrong, and nothing raises.

- Site: https://wrong-numbers.dev/
- Contact: arthi1805@gmail.com
- GitHub: https://github.com/arthi-arumugam-git
- Field guide: https://github.com/arthi-arumugam-git/wrong-numbers
- Tools that came out of this work: whatbroke (https://github.com/arthi-arumugam-git/whatbroke), cachecheck (https://github.com/arthi-arumugam-git/cachecheck), billproof (https://arthi-arumugam-git.github.io/billproof/), stockproof (https://arthi-arumugam-git.github.io/stockproof/)

## Services

All fixed scope, fixed fee, no retainer.

### Is the score right?
- Eval integrity audit, from $5,000: scorer and metric correctness including empty denominators, LLM-as-judge parsing and scales, truncated output scored as an answer, ground-truth alignment and sample counts; findings report, a fix for each, and a regression test.
- Eval suite build, from $10,000: an eval suite around a product's real failure modes, with ground-truth data, judges whose parsing fails closed, and metrics that report nan rather than 0.0 when nothing was measured.
- Agent regression gates, from $5,000: CI gates that diff agent runs by tool calls, arguments, outputs, latency and cost, built on whatbroke.

### Is the bill right?
- Cost reconciliation audit, from $5,000: every provider, every cache path, every multiplier in a billing or metering codebase, checked against the provider's invoice; findings as failing tests.
- Revenue assurance, $10,000: the same for a product that bills its own customers per token, reconciling metered usage against customer invoices, under-billing, over-billing and cost basis.
